title: Direction-Dependent Rotation Error and Calibration Trade-offs in Sparse-IMU Gait Estimation
description: Reproducibility archive for the analysis of two-sensor gait-kinematics estimation under imposed sensor-frame rotations. The release preserves the frozen virtual-IMU input (747 gait cycles from 138 participants), original Ridge model code, and external physical-IMU protocol summaries (248 windows from 19 participants). Expanded analyses examine augmentation-seed and participant-partition stability, walking-speed ablation, nested physical-cohort regularization, directional and matched-relative-angle perturbations, and calibration estimated from records disjoint from evaluation. The directional analyses show that the same relative rotation magnitude can yield substantially different errors depending on the local rotation axis and sensor configuration. Post-rotation frame calibration can reduce adverse errors with an accuracy cost in the unrotated condition. The two ZIP files under r2_reanalysis/artifacts contain the later-stage executed code and detailed analysis results. Physical remounting experiments and raw C3D-to-derived-input reconstruction are not claimed. The original raw Camargo dataset is available from the source repository and is not redistributed.

creators.name: Lima Júnior, Sérgio de Nazaré Rodrigues
